cards.claim: AOL pre-conditioning enables removal of one Newton-Schulz iteration while maintaining competitive polar error
cards.conditions: Random matrices (16-2048), Newton-Schulz with 5 iterations baseline
cards.effect: Reduction in polar error from 0.25→0.12 (Turbo-Muon 4-iter vs Muon 5-iter baseline) with cumulative 2.83× speedup on orthogonalization step
cards.evidence: Empirical measurements on synthetic matrices and Table 1 ablation study
cards.quote: Importantly, our approach lowers the polar error enough to allow the removal of one iteration (Turbo-Muon iter=4), while still achieving a competitive or improved polar error.

cards.claim: Turbo-Muon acts as drop-in replacement for Muon achieving training time reduction while preserving performance
cards.conditions: CIFAR-10 speed-run, NanoGPT 144M on FineWeb, ImageNet-1K training
cards.effect: End-to-end training time reduced by 0.8-3.6% (CIFAR-10: 1.359→1.348s, NanoGPT: 273.8→266.0s, ImageNet: 422m→407m) with equivalent final performance
cards.quote: Empirically, Turbo-Muon acts as a drop-in replacement for Muon, consistently reducing training time by up to 4% while preserving downstream performance across diverse settings

cards.claim: AOL pre-conditioning reduces initial polar error initialization without additional matrix multiplications
cards.conditions: Matrix sizes 16-2048 with standard normal distribution sampling (32 matrices per size)
cards.effect: Polar error improvement shown in Fig. 3(a); overhead characterized as 'negligible for large matrices: matrix–vector multiplication is cheaper than matrix–matrix multiplication'
cards.evidence: Empirical comparison in Fig. 3(a) and ablation Table 1 showing unchanged runtime for AOL step alone
cards.quote: Crucially, this reuses the Gram computation and avoids any additional matrix multiplications. AOL pre-conditioning thus incurs negligible runtime overhead

cards.claim: Turbo-Muon orthogonalization reduces from ~130ms to ~46ms (4 iterations) on 4096×4096 matrices
cards.conditions: 4096×4096 matrices, PyTorch implementation with Triton kernels, 5→4 iteration reduction plus AOL and fused Triton kernel improvements

cards.claim: Turbo-Muon update direction remains steepest descent under induced norm despite modified pre-conditioning target
cards.conditions: Theoretical analysis with diagonal positive-bounded rescaling matrix
cards.effect: Projected update remains 'aligned' with raw gradient, ensuring strict descent direction despite convergence to modified target
cards.quote: Meaning that the projected update recovered by Turbo-Muon is always 'aligned' with the raw gradient. Thus, it yields a strict descent direction.

cards.claim: AOL pre-conditioning effectiveness increases with matrix size
cards.conditions: Random matrices from normal distribution, sizes 16–2048
cards.effect: Convergence speed improvement 'especially for large matrices', enabling iteration removal with maintained polar error (Fig. 3a)
cards.quote: Pre-conditioning is effective for large matrices: Applying AOL before the algorithm improves convergence speed, especially for large matrices.

cards.claim: Muon+ (with Triton kernels and dynamic polynomial factors) achieves ~1.69× speedup over baseline Muon with dynamic coefficients
cards.effect: Muon baseline 130ms → dynamic coefficients unchanged → Muon+ 77ms (1.69× speedup)

cards.claim: Heavy-tailed gradient distributions do not invalidate AOL pre-conditioning convergence improvements
cards.conditions: Matrices sampled from heavy-tailed Levy distribution (tail indices 1.5-2.0), stress-test scenario for gradient-like matrices
cards.effect: AOL convergence improvements remain valid despite realistic heavy-tailed gradient statistics
cards.quote: In App. B, we conduct additional experiments on matrices sampled from a heavy-tailed Levy distribution, and show that the conclusions of our empirical convergence experiments remain valid in these settings.
